correctness.rationale: The proof fixes all norms and exact domain, reconstructs the spectral/Lorentz projection map, explicitly differentiates the indefinite open sector, and uses affine endpoint interpolation to control every Jacobian. Absolute row and column sums give the sharp 3/2 in independent-entry infinity and sum norms; the oblique rank-one Hilbert projection calculation gives squared Euclidean norm at most 9/8. Integrating on generic segments and applying continuity gives the global bound; one exact finite pair and two families of smooth approaching points give the lower bounds. Python stdlib verification replayed 15731 assertions, including exact rational identities, without pretending finite tests prove continuum inequalities.

originality.rationale: The inspected Sun–Sun 2002 and Shapiro 2002 full-text treatments state Frobenius spectral projection, semismoothness and matrix derivative ingredients, and Andreev 2014 supplies a general oblique-projection lemma, but none supplies the optimized independent-entry coordinate Lipschitz constants. Natural standard-coordinate Lorentz-cone constants are inequivalent because its Frobenius isometry is not an isometry for independent matrix-entry norms. Searches for alias statements and stronger claims found no direct covering result. A more general historical theorem might still imply the three constants; no exhaustive priority claim.

value.rationale: Independent symmetric entries are the naturally observed degrees of freedom in 2x2 matrix reconstruction and constrained spectral truncation. Their ell_p error norms differ from Frobenius, making exact stability beyond Hilbert nonexpansivity a substantive question. The theorem completely determines the globally optimal constants for three canonical norms, exhibits 50% sensitivity inflation in two of them, supplies sharp extremal configurations, and derives an oblique-projector mechanism which may inform higher-dimensional studies. It does not claim higher-dimensional or all-exponent extensions.
